scope.description: A focused direction based on El Lissitzky's Proun works from 1919–1927, where flat color planes and geometric volumes share an imagined, quasi- architectural space. Consistent axonometric cues and controlled color contrast create the sense that forms can float above, below, and through one another. This direction describes a specific artist-led transition between painting and architecture, not all Constructivism or a literal building method.
limitations: Preserve the user-supplied subject, objects, relationships, and requested level of abstraction; do not default to red squares, slogans, stars, or political symbols.
Use axonometric or oblique depth only when it clarifies the requested composition; keep a coherent spatial reference instead of mixing arbitrary projections.
Suggest a transition between flat and volumetric form through image relationships; do not imply that the generated image is a physically buildable model.

rules.applies_when: The requested image uses abstraction or stylized geometry to suggest space.
rules.instruction: Combine clearly flat color planes with a few geometric volumes that share the same imagined space; let overlap, partial occlusion, or edge continuity imply depth without turning the image into either a flat poster or a literal realistic room.
rules.observable: The viewer can distinguish planes from volumes and understand how they relate spatially, while the overall image remains an intentional constructed field.
rules.reject_when: All forms lie on one graphic layer, every shape becomes a fully shaded 3D object, or unrelated forms appear to occupy incompatible spaces.
rules.avoid: flat poster-only treatment, photorealistic rooms, and random floating geometry

rules.applies_when: The composition includes geometric blocks or volumes arranged in imagined space.
rules.instruction: Establish a small consistent set of oblique or axonometric directions and use them to organize overlaps, visible faces, and apparent movement; allow forms to float, but keep their orientation legible.
rules.observable: Directional edges agree enough to imply one constructed spatial field, and overlapping forms remain distinguishable.
rules.reject_when: Projection axes contradict one another without an intentional focal shift, or depth relies only on drop shadows.
rules.avoid: incompatible vanishing points, random rotation, and shadow-only depth

rules.applies_when: The requested direction uses color planes to distinguish parts of a constructed space.
rules.instruction: Assign contrasting colors to selected planes or volumes so they clarify overlap, orientation, or visual force; maintain a restrained neutral field where needed and follow the user's palette if specified.
rules.observable: Color helps identify spatial roles and directional movement without becoming a universal red-black-white formula.
rules.reject_when: Saturation is decorative, colors ignore the form boundaries, or an unrequested political or typographic symbol is introduced.
rules.avoid: fixed red-square motifs, global color filters, and text-led composition
